narrative.notes: Third-person limited on Elias Vane only. No other minds. Expansions must keep this POV.

fog_kitchen.title: Breakfast in Fogglass
fog_kitchen.body:
Salt fog presses the kitchen window until the glass looks like milk. Elias Vane eats toast that tastes faintly of metal—always has, in Maskward—and watches his foster mother hum while she butters nothing in particular.

His foster father checks a wristwatch that does not tick. The second hand is painted on.

Ren Kade texts from across the hall building: *tram in ten. don't be weird today.*

Something in the room is almost right. Almost is the word that keeps catching on Elias's teeth.

choices.text: Ask Why the Watch Never Ticks
Eat Quietly and Leave for Class
Text Ren That Something Feels Off

tram_glitch.title: The Tram Window
tram_glitch.body:
The harbor tram climbs the ridge on wet rails. Outside, Maskward's towers wear fog like borrowed coats. Inside, passengers smile with the same delay, as if an invisible conductor cues their faces.

Elias catches his reflection in the window. For half a second, the glass shows a second outline behind a woman in a green coat—too tall, jointed wrong, smiling through her.

Then the outline is gone. The woman meets his eyes and the smile settles into place, perfect and late.

Ren elbows him. "You're staring. People hate that."

The tram brakes. Fog spills through the doors like a soft animal.

choices.text: Follow the Woman in Green Off the Tram
Tell Ren Exactly What He Saw
Look Away and Pretend It Was Sleep

lecture_hall.title: Civic Biology 101
lecture_hall.body:
In the lecture hall, Professor Hale draws a human silhouette and fills it with tidy organs. The chalk squeaks. Somewhere above the rafters, water drips in a rhythm that does not match the rain.

Elias's notes refuse to stay notes. The silhouette on the board briefly grows a second jaw. No one else reacts.

Ren's pencil keeps moving. His knuckles are the wrong temperature when they brush Elias's sleeve—cool as quay stone.

This is the hour the city usually forgives. Today it feels hungry.

choices.text: Stand and Ask What the Second Jaw Means
Keep Copying Notes and Survive the Hour
Slip Out Early and Trail Ren

almost_taken.title: The Service Stair
almost_taken.body:
The service stair smells of bleach and wet fur. Elias barely finishes a breath before the green-coated woman is there—closer than footsteps allow—mouth opening past the shape of a mouth.

He understands, without being told, that he has been seen seeing.

Something inside him answers: not light, not heat—Residue, a pressure like held breath turning into weight. Time he has already survived thickens behind his ribs.

He does not know the word yet. He only knows he is still alive one second longer than he should be.

choices.text: Burn the New Weight and Shove Free
Freeze and Hope It Mistakes Him for Prey Too Dull
Scream for Ren or Anyone

mira_alley.title: Mira in the Rain Spout
mira_alley.body:
A silver flare cracks the stairwell. The green coat folds wrong and flees into a vent that should not take a body.

A young woman in a rain-dark coat lowers a chalk-marked baton. "Elias Vane. Orphan file. Foster house on Fogglass. Congratulations: you noticed."

She is Mira Solenne—Compass Guild scout, voice flat as a tide chart. "Most humans die in the noticing. You banked Residue instead. Live longer awake, and it thickens. Spend it, and it thins. That is the only kindness this city offers."

Rain needles the alley. Far off, a tram bell sounds almost human.

choices.text: Tell Mira Everything He Saw Today
Give Her Half the Truth and Watch Her
Demand Proof Before He Moves

salt_pier.title: Salt Pier Briefing
salt_pier.body:
At Salt Pier the fog thins just enough to show cranes like gallows. Mira sketches Maskward on a damp napkin: rings of districts, a black X under the old civic gate, tiny dots labeled *clear*—true humans.

"One in thousands," she says. "The rest wear faces. They call themselves citizens. We call them Masked when we are being polite."

Elias thinks of toast that tasted like metal. Of a watch that never ticked. Of Ren's cool knuckles.

"The Compass Guild keeps a ledger of the living," Mira continues. "If you want a chance, you take their trial. If you want a grave, you go home and pretend the stair was a nightmare."

Gulls scream like torn paper.

choices.text: Agree to the Compass Trial
Ask First Whether His Family Are Masked
Hesitate Until Mira Starts Walking Anyway

compass_trial.title: The Compass Trial
compass_trial.body:
The Compass Guild occupies a warehouse that smells of oil and old paper. A circle of chalk, three sealed jars, one blindfold. The examiner's smile is human enough that Elias almost trusts it—then notices the man's shadow has too many fingers.

"Find which jar holds a true heartbeat," the examiner says. "Lie, and the Masked in the walls will smell your panic."

Residue ticks behind Elias's sternum like a second clock. Mira watches from the rail, baton across her knees.

Outside, fog taps the loading doors in patient code.

choices.text: Spend Residue to Feel the True Pulse
Choose by Logic and Luck Alone
Watch the Examiner's Shadow for a Tell

chalk_map.title: Map Room
chalk_map.body:
Accepted—provisionally. The map room is a cathedral of street grids. Red pins mark disappearances. Blue pins mark hunters. Black pins mark places the Guild will not name aloud.

Captain Orr of the Compass speaks without looking up. "Canal district. Something has been nesting under the flower market. You go with Solenne. Bring back proof, not poetry."

Elias's badge is still warm from the stamp. It feels like a target as much as a key.

Ren's unanswered texts glow on his phone like small accusations.

choices.text: Take the Canal Assignment Without Complaint
Ask What the Black Pins Mean
Text Ren Before He Goes Into the Dark

canal_hunt.title: Flower Market Canal
canal_hunt.body:
Petals float on black water. The flower market's night shift never ends in Maskward; buyers come with wet coats and dry eyes. Under the quay boards, something breathes in time with the tide.

Mira signals left. Elias's Residue rises like fever. He can burn it for speed, for a harder strike, for one more second of not dying.

A Masked vendor turns, face slipping half an inch toward something antlered and wrong.

This is no longer theory.

choices.text: Burn Residue and Strike First
Hold Back and Let Mira Lead the Bind
Shout a Warning to the Crowd First

ren_bridge.title: Ren on the Iron Bridge
ren_bridge.body:
They find Ren on the iron footbridge above the canal, hands in his pockets, smiling the old smile. Behind him the fog thins and shows the truth for three merciless seconds: not a boy—a long, jointed thing wearing a boy like a coat.

"You weren't supposed to wake," Ren says gently. "I liked you better sleeping."

Elias's childhood rewrites itself in the space between heartbeats. Shared lunches. Shared silence. Shared lies he never knew were lies.

Mira's baton hums. "Your call, Vane. Proof, mercy, or leverage."

choices.text: Spare Ren and Let Him Run
Force the Mask Off for Guild Proof
Bind Ren as Reluctant Informant

supper_masks.title: Supper on Fogglass
supper_masks.body:
Home still smells like metal toast. His foster parents have set three places. The fourth chair—Ren's old chair—is already pushed in.

"You look tired," his foster mother says, and her mouth is almost the right shape.

Elias understands the house now: a careful habitat. Kindness as husbandry. He can sit, burn Residue to keep his face calm, or shatter the evening and see what feeds beneath the wallpaper.

Outside, fog presses fingerprints into the glass.

choices.text: Sit, Eat, and Bank Residue in Silence
Confront Them With What He Knows
Leave Without Eating and Do Not Look Back

archive_rain.title: Archive Under Rain
archive_rain.body:
Mira's archive is a basement of drowned filing cabinets. She lays out photocopies: Veiled Court seals, Compass kill quotas, a third mark—Pale Lattice—stamped on smuggled paper.

"Lattice hates the Guild's pageantry," Mira says. "They harvest Masked for parts and call it math. Compass hates Lattice's appetite. Both hate the Courts. You are about to be asked to pick a hatred you can live inside."

Rain finds the window well and drums. Elias's badge feels heavier.

He can give Mira the whole of his fear, or keep a private ledger.

choices.text: Trust Mira With the Whole Fear
Keep a Private Ledger of Doubts
Ask Her Straight About Pale Lattice

crimson_bulletin.title: Crimson Fog Bulletin
crimson_bulletin.body:
City speakers crackle at noon. A calm voice announces Crimson Fog Week: voluntary curfews, extra ferries, "weather enrichment." On the Guild floor, nobody pretends it is weather.

Captain Orr taps the map's black pins. "The Veiled Courts open their hunting calendar. Districts go soft. We go hard. Provisional members who flinch are statistics."

Elias feels Residue pool like warm ink. Surviving has made him denser. Denseness is not the same as ready.

Mira mouths one word: *quay.*

choices.text: Volunteer for the Front Teams
Request Intel Duty Beside Mira
Prep Quietly and Watch Who Lies Loudest

foreign_quay.title: Foreign Quay
foreign_quay.body:
Foreign Quay smells of diesel and spice crates. Sailors argue in languages the fog tries to erase. A Masked customs officer stamps papers with a hand that has too many quiet bones.

Here the city admits it is larger than Fogglass and the lecture hall. Ships bring other hungers. One crate leaks black salt that hisses when rain touches it.

Mira buys information with cigarettes and silence. Elias learns that Crimson Fog Week is not only slaughter—it is census. The Courts count who still pretends.

A child on the quay waves at him with a perfect, delayed smile.

choices.text: Buy the Smuggled Court Chart
Shadow the Customs Officer
Steer the Child Away From the Soft Crowd

lattice_whisper.title: Pale Lattice Whisper
lattice_whisper.body:
In a tea shop that serves no tea, a Lattice agent slides a coin across the table. One face is blank. The other is etched with a grid.

"Compass will spend you like chalk," the agent murmurs. "Lattice pays in outcomes. Join before Crimson Week peaks, and we teach you to spend Residue without their sermons."

Mira is not at the table. Elias came alone—or thinks he did. The shop's mirror shows a second him half a second late.

The coin is cold enough to burn.

choices.text: Take the Coin and Hear Their Terms
Refuse and Report the Approach
Pocket the Coin Silent Without Promising

loyalty_drill.title: Loyalty Drill
loyalty_drill.body:
Captain Orr lines the provisionals in the warehouse. "Crimson Week needs clean chains of command. Speak now if Lattice kissed your ear."

Eyes move. Nobody breathes honestly. Elias feels the coin—or the absence of it—like a fever.

Orr's gaze stops on him. "Vane. Canal proof was adequate. Home situation is flagged. Will you obey a kill order on a foster roof if the ledger demands it?"

The question is a blade with two handles.

choices.text: Vow to Obey the Ledger
Vow to Protect Humans First, Ledger Second
Stay Silent Until Orr Moves On

fracture_hall.title: Fracture Hall
fracture_hall.body:
Arguments become architecture. Half the Guild wants quarantine fire across Fogglass. The other half wants bargains with lesser Courts. Mira's jaw is tight enough to crack chalk.

Elias sees the shape of the next year: chalk badges, Lattice grids, or something that is not either—an Ash Circlet of hunters who answer to the living, not the ledger.

Ren's possible shadow hangs in the rafters of his mind. Residue waits like a held match.

This is the hallway where careers end and myths begin.

choices.text: Found the Ash Circlet With Mira If She Will Follow
Take the Pale Lattice Pact
Stay Compass and Fight From Inside

circlet_roof.title: Ash Circlet Roof
circlet_roof.body:
They gather on a water-tank roof: Mira, two burnt-out Compass scouts, a quay medic who still believes in stitches. Elias draws a circle in ash and rain.

"No quotas," he says, and hears how young it sounds. "No farming the Masked for parts. We keep clearbloods alive through Crimson Week, then we argue about the world."

Mira nods once. "Then we will be hunted by everyone with a stamp."

Below them, fog districts blink into curfew red.

choices.text: Seal the Circlet and Prepare for Veil Week
Risk One More Night Recruiting Quietly

lattice_cell.title: Lattice Cell
lattice_cell.body:
Pale Lattice keeps its maps in a refrigerated room. Numbers replace names. A surgeon-captain explains Residue expenditure like interest.

"Mercy is a rounding error," she says. "Survive Crimson Week with us, and Maskward becomes a spreadsheet that bleeds less."

Elias's Circlet-shaped hope goes quiet. The coin's blank face finally makes sense.

Somewhere above, Compass sirens begin a different hymn.

choices.text: Accept the Cell's Crimson Deployment
Accept—but Smuggle Mira a Warning

guild_inner.title: Inside the Compass
guild_inner.body:
Staying means corridors, stamps, and Orr's voice in his sleep. Elias is given a cleaner badge and a dirtier list.

Mira remains nearby—not always approving, always counting exits. "If you stay, make the ledger lie in the right direction," she says.

Crimson Fog Week begins with a sound like a wet flag.

Elias banks Residue the way other people bank apologies.

choices.text: Take Inner Roster for Veil Week
Rewrite One Kill Order Into an Evacuation

veil_week.title: Crimson Fog Week
veil_week.body:
The fog arrives the color of diluted blood. Streetlamps halo wrong. Neighbors knock with gifts and teeth.

Wherever Elias stands—Circlet roof, Lattice cell, or Compass hall—the city becomes a throat. Residue thickens each hour he remains upright and awake. Clarity frays each hour he must decide who is still human enough to save.

Reports contradict. A ferry sinks and then is seen docked. A school rings its bell at 3:17 for twelve minutes.

Mira's message, if it reaches him, is three words: *under gate soon.*

choices.text: Spend Residue to Clear One Housing Block
Hunt an Elite Masked Through the Fog
Hold a Defensive Line and Bank More Residue

court_banner.title: Court Banner on High Street
court_banner.body:
A Veiled Court emissary walks High Street without hurry. Its banner is a sheet of fog stitched with faces. Where it passes, advertisements rewrite into invitations.

"Census," it announces in a voice like polite radio. "Clearbloods may register for gentle endings. Hunters may register for instructive ones."

Elias's faction—whatever stamp he carries—tightens around the moment. Guns and chalk and grids all feel small.

He can challenge, bargain, or vanish into side streets toward the under-gate.

choices.text: Challenge the Emissary in the Open
Break for the Under-Gate via Side Streets
Feign Registration to Steal Court Timing
Offer the Emissary a Bargain of Masks

alley_war.title: War of Alleys
alley_war.body:
Alleys become borders. Compass chalk meets Lattice cable meets Circlet ash marks. Civilians—if the word still holds—run between doctrines.

Elias fights until his hands shake. Residue is a dwindling treasury. He sees Ren once, or thinks he does, at the far end of a lane: a wave that might be farewell or targeting.

Mira appears at his shoulder smelling of rain and copper. "The under-gate is open. The Courts are using Crimson Week to feed something older than badges."

Smoke writes false street names on the sky.

choices.text: Push With Mira Toward the Under-Gate
Stay Behind to Cover a Civilian Corridor
Cut Solo Through the Roofs

under_gate.title: The Under-Gate
under_gate.body:
Beneath civic stone, the under-gate is a mouth of rivets and old law. Beyond it, something like an ocean turns without water. Masks hang on hooks that cast no shadows.

Here Residue rings loud. Elias understands the city's secret grammar: Maskward is not a hometown. It is a holding pattern. The Courts thin human noise so the older dark can sleep, or wake.

Mira's baton hangs unused. "We can seal it with enough Residue and clarity. Or we can walk away and let the Week finish its math."

The gate breathes. Waiting.

choices.text: Study the Gate Before Touching It
Touch the Gate and Feel Its Hunger
Listen to Mira's Full Plan First

last_counsel.title: Last Counsel
last_counsel.body:
There is little time and less clean language. Elias stands in the rivet dark with whatever allies his choices still allow.

He can pour Residue into a final stand—seal, crown, or burn—or keep enough to flee on the morning ferries when fog lightens to ordinary gray.

Clarity tells him what he is. Residue tells him what he can still buy. Trust and stamps tell him who will still stand when the buying starts.

The gate's breath fogs his eyelashes.

choices.text: Commit to a Final Stand at the Gate
Refuse the Stand and Plan Extraction
Split Efforts: Half Seal, Half Evacuate
Open Himself to the Fog and Stop Fighting Clarity

fog_reckoning.title: Fog Reckoning
fog_reckoning.body:
Crimson Week breaks like a fever—or pretends to. What remains of Elias's path gathers into one weather: Circlet ash, Lattice grid, Compass chalk, or the lone ember of a boy who noticed too much.

He does not get a speech from the city. He gets consequence.

The fog listens for which ending he has earned.

choices.text: Step Into Whatever Comes

ending_circlet_dawn.title: Circlet Dawn
ending_circlet_dawn.body:
Ash marks outlast the Crimson banners. The Ash Circlet holds three districts through the worst nights, then a fourth by rumor alone. Mira lives. Elias's Residue runs thin, but the living count higher than the ledger ever did.

Maskward does not become kind. It becomes, in places, defended.

At dawn the fog turns ordinary gray, and for the first time since the stairwell, Elias sleeps without listening for a painted second hand.

ending_guild_crown.title: Compass Crown
ending_guild_crown.body:
Elias never leaves the Compass. He bends it. Kill orders soften into corridors; Orr's ledger gains inconvenient footnotes written in a steady hand.

The Guild calls it reform when it works and insubordination when it does not. Either way, Fogglass keeps more of its clearbloods than the Courts budgeted for.

On a quiet morning, Elias corrects a map pin and feels—almost—like a citizen of something real.

ending_lattice_ledger.title: Lattice Ledger
ending_lattice_ledger.body:
Pale Lattice's grid closes over Maskward like netting. Crimson Week becomes a harvest with better margins. Elias learns to speak in outcomes until mercy sounds like inefficiency even to himself.

The city bleeds less loudly. It does not bleed less.

At night he dreams of blank coins and wakes counting breaths as inventory.

ending_mask_bargain.title: Bargain of Masks
ending_mask_bargain.body:
The fighting ends in contracts. Some Masked keep their faces; some hunters keep their badges; the Courts keep the under-gate ajar.

Elias survives as a translator between hungers. Ren—if spared or not—becomes a rumor that smiles from tram glass.

It is peace the way a scar is skin.

ending_quiet_ferry.title: Quiet Ferry
ending_quiet_ferry.body:
He leaves on a ferry that claims to exit the fog's jurisdiction. Whether that is true is a problem for another coastline.

Maskward shrinks into a red weather behind him. Mira's last look—if she gave one—stays unreadable in third-person dark.

Elias banks no more Residue. He banks distance, and hopes distance is a kind of clarity.

ending_gate_seal.title: Gate Seal
ending_gate_seal.body:
He pours Residue into the under-gate until his hands go numb and the rivets scream shut. Clarity holds the pattern; his body pays the interest.

The Courts howl without mouths. Crimson Week stutters. Maskward will invent new hungers later—but not today.

They find Elias seated against the sealed iron, still breathing, already becoming a story the Guild will misquote.

ending_hollow_truce.title: Hollow Truce
ending_hollow_truce.body:
Sirens end. Banners drop. No faction wins enough to brag cleanly. Elias stands in the leftover quiet with middling Residue and a city that agrees, for now, to pretend.

People return to metal toast and delayed smiles. He returns to work that is not quite peace.

The fog remains. It always does.

ending_lone_ember.title: Lone Ember
ending_lone_ember.body:
Power without a circle is still power. Elias's Residue makes alleys flinch. Hunters ask his advice and do not stay for tea.

He keeps Maskward's worst nights from swallowing whole blocks—and comes home to no voice saying his name correctly.

An ember can light a street. It cannot be a hearth.

ending_fog_eat.title: The Fog Eats
ending_fog_eat.body:
Clarity fails like a wet match. Faces swim. The city's true angles arrive without kindness.

Whether the Courts take him, or the stairwell's hunger finally finishes its meal, the story from outside is the same: another provisional light gone out in Crimson weather.

Fog closes over the place where Elias Vane was learning to see.
